name: Yam Rot (Soft Rot / Dry Rot)
scientificName: Botryodiplodia theobromae / Fusarium spp. / Penicillium spp.
description: A complex of fungal and bacterial rots affecting yam tubers both in the field and during storage. They cause significant post-harvest losses, which can exceed 30% in traditional storage systems in West Africa.
symptoms: Soft, water-soaked areas on tubers (wet rot)
Dry, sunken lesions on tuber surface (dry rot)
Internal discoloration spreading from outer tissue inward
Brown or black fungal growth on tuber surface
Completely decayed tubers collapsing into a soft mass
causes: Botryodiplodia theobromae, Fusarium spp., Penicillium spp., Erwinia spp.
Mechanical damage during harvest and handling
Wounds from insect and nematode damage
High humidity and temperature during storage
Harvesting immature yams with thin skin
treatments: Remove and discard rotted tubers immediately to prevent spread
Sort healthy from infected tubers before storage
Cure tubers in a well-ventilated area for 1-2 weeks before storage
Apply wood ash or lime powder to cut surfaces
prevention: Harvest yams carefully to avoid bruising and cuts
Allow tubers to mature fully before harvest
Cure harvested yams at 30-35°C with ventilation for 7-10 days
Store in well-ventilated barns or yam sheds
Treat cut setts with wood ash before planting
Maintain good hygiene in storage structures
